problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 0 \\ -8 & 9 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 & a \\ 1 & 0 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $a+2b.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}15 & -4 & -16 \\ 40 & -5 & -40 \\ -10 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ & 0 \\ 4 & ∗ & -4 \\ -1 & ∗ & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the second column of  the matrix $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=15,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=5.$ 

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get
Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}A-{\lambda }_{2}I & =[\begin{aligned}15 & -4 & -16 \\ 40 & -5 & -40 \\ -10 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -4 & -16 \\ 40 & -4 & -40 \\ -10 & 1 & 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ that we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}16 & -4 & -16 & 0 \\ 40 & -4 & -40 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{16}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{4} & -1 & 0 \\ 40 & -4 & -40 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-40{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{4} & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$
Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -4 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$
